stdout.text:
Extract UMI from FASTQ reads into the read name

Usage: <BIN> extract [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -I, --stdin <FILE>
          Input FASTQ (gzip by .gz suffix; omit or - for stdin) [alias: --input]
  -S, --stdout <FILE>
          Output FASTQ (omit or - for stdout) [alias: --output]
      --read2-in <FILE>
          Paired read 2 input
      --read2-out <FILE>
          Paired read 2 output
  -p, --bc-pattern <PATTERN>
          Barcode pattern; N marks a UMI base
      --bc-pattern2 <PATTERN>
          Barcode pattern for read 2
      --extract-method <METHOD>
          Extraction method: string [default: string]
      --verbose
          Print detailed build information together with --version
      --3prime
          Barcode is on the 3' end of the read
      --quality-filter-threshold <QUALITY_FILTER_THRESHOLD>
          Discard reads with a UMI base quality below this value
      --quality-filter-mask <QUALITY_FILTER_MASK>
          Mask UMI bases below this quality with N
      --quality-encoding <ENCODING>
          Quality score encoding: phred33, phred64 or solexa [default: phred33]
      --umi-separator <UMI_SEPARATOR>
          Separator between the read name and the UMI [default: _]
      --quiet
          Suppress informational output
  -L, --log <FILE>
          Log file (defaults to stderr)
  -h, --help
          Print help

EXAMPLES:
  <BIN> extract -I reads.fastq.gz -S out.fastq.gz -p NNNN
  <BIN> extract -I r1.fastq -S o1.fastq -p NNNN --read2-in r2.fastq --read2-out o2.fastq

NOTES:
  N marks UMI bases in the barcode pattern; the whole pattern is removed from the read.
  The UMI is appended to the read name with --umi-separator (default _).
  gzip is selected by a .gz suffix; omit -I/-S for stdin/stdout.
